messages.content:
Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Older adults in the second, third and fourth serum 25(OH)D quartiles had 18-22% lower depressive symptom scores than those in the lowest quartile.
Sentence: "Fully adjusted models indicated a 22 % (RR 0.78, 95 % CI 0.68-0.89), 21 % (RR 0.79, 95 % CI 0.68-0.90), and 18 % (RR 0.82, 95 % CI 0.71-0.95) lower score of depressive symptoms in people in the second, third, and fourth 25(OH)D quartiles, when compared to people in the first quartile (P for trend <0.0001)."
Measured as: depressive symptom score (15-point Geriatric Depression Scale)
Population: 2839 Dutch older adults aged 65 years and older
Intervention: Serum 25(OH)D concentration by quartile (observational exposure)
Comparator: Lowest 25(OH)D quartile
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 2,839
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: harm
Claim: In PD patients given vitamin D3, folic acid and B12 for 6 months, the 15D depression dimension score significantly increased (improved) from baseline.
Sentence: "After the intervention, the mean score of speech, mental function, discomfort and symptoms, depression, and QoL significantly increased (p < 0.05 for all)."
Measured as: depression (15D dimension score)
Population: Levodopa-treated Parkinson's disease patients in Romania, mean age 71 years
Intervention: Daily tablet with 800 IU vitamin D3, 1000 µg folic acid, 15 µg vitamin B12 for 6 months
Comparator: None (single-arm, baseline vs 6 months)
Design: case series
Sample size: not reported
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Both findings bear on vitamin D and depressive symptoms, but a cohort of Dutch older adults linking higher serum 25(OH)D to lower GDS scores is observational, while the single-arm case series of PD patients on a vitamin D3/folate/B12 combination reports a before-after change in a 15D dimension with no control.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"design_or_bias","also_differs":["population","intervention","comparator","outcome_measure"],"detail":"design: cohort of 2,839 older adults (serum level exposure) vs uncontrolled single-arm case series of Parkinson's patients on combined D3+folic acid+B12 for 6 months"}
